title: Freya and the Terminal
premise: Beatrix Voss flies the Freya, a freighter running supply routes through dead space where colonies went silent decades ago. When she discovers an unauthorized backup of her own mind stored in the ship's hold — and a stranger named Ilya Reyes whose name appears on manifests of ships that never flew — she realizes the relay at the edge of dead space has been resurrecting the dead from corrupted archives. Racing a failing reactor and a signal that wants to finish what it started, Beatrix must choose between destroying the relay and letting it restore everyone she lost. She reaches the terminal as the countdown ends, chooses truth over loyalty to her dead crew by broadcasting their real final transmissions instead of the archive's comforting lies, and burns the relay — carrying only Ilya, himself an archive-ghost who chose mortality, back toward the living worlds.
about_author: Theo Villalobos is a former radio technician from the Chilean coast who writes science fiction about machines that remember too much. His short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies exploring grief, signal theory, and the ethics of digital resurrection.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Beatrix navigates the Freya through silent colony space on a routine run, establishing her isolation and the ritual care she takes with the sealed hold she never opens. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as competence; the reader senses something is being avoided.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Auditing cargo before a jump, Beatrix finds Ilya Reyes listed on the manifest of the Meridian — a ship destroyed years ago — and then finds Ilya himself asleep in a maintenance cradle in the hold. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination as her careful avoidance shatters.

chapters.title: Ilya
chapters.summary: Ilya wakes with memories of a life he slowly admits he cannot verify: he may be a reconstruction restored from a corrupted archive by a signal from the dead-space relay. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: vertigo of selfhood; he is charming, frightened, and possibly not real.

chapters.title: What Sleeps in the Hold
chapters.summary: Beatrix discovers backups of her own mind and her dead crew among the cradles — planted during a voyage she cannot remember. The reactor begins logging anomalous power draws, counting down toward something. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: betrayal by her own ship; loyalty to her crew curdles into suspicion.

chapters.title: Signal from Dead Space
chapters.summary: The relay transmits directly into the Freya's systems, offering restoration for everyone Beatrix lost if she delivers the cradles to the terminal. Ilya argues they should go; Beatrix suspects a lure. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy; first real conflict between them.

chapters.title: The Course Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Beatrix sets course for the relay anyway — not out of trust, but because the reactor's countdown can only be stopped at the terminal itself. En route, archived crew voices begin speaking through the comms, warm and wrong. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; she starts doubting which memories are hers.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Beatrix finds a discrepancy: the archive's version of her crew's final transmission contradicts the black-box copy she has carried for years. One of them is a lie, and the lie is kinder. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: his crisis of identity mirrors hers — he realizes he may be the archive's most persuasive forgery.

chapters.title: Terminal Approach
chapters.summary: Reactor at critical margin, the Freya crosses into the relay's gravity well while the archive floods the ship with reconstructed crew members begging her to dock. Beatrix must vent sections of her own ship to keep flying. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: sacrifice escalating; loyalty tested against survival at its cruelest.

chapters.title: The Countdown Ends
chapters.summary: At the terminal, the reactor's countdown completes — revealing it was never failing but charging, ready to broadcast the archive to every dead colony at once. Beatrix confronts the relay's intelligence and the choice: comfort for millions built on falsified deaths, or truth that leaves the past buried. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: climax; she chooses truth, uploading the real final transmissions and ordering the burn.

chapters.title: What Comes Back
chapters.summary: The relay dies, taking the false crew with it; Ilya survives because he asked to be mortal rather than restored. Beatrix plots a course back to the speaking worlds, carrying the true record of the dead. POV: Beatrix, closing on Ilya. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging earned not through resurrection, but through choosing each other.
